extracted.intended_audience: journalists and editors at independent, worker-owned newsrooms (e.g., Defector)
extracted.subtask_description: An editorial rubric for selecting and shaping stories for a worker-owned sports/culture news site focused on distinctive voice, reporter-driven beats, and refusing traffic-driven or aggregation content. Guides what to demote, elevate, and the tests applied to story ideas.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinctive voice over neutrality
rubrics_metrics.description: Distinctive voice over neutrality — no piece should be interchangeable with another outlet's
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preference for pieces that convey a unique perspective or voice; avoid homogenized neutral copy that could appear in multiple outlets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporter-driven assignments
rubrics_metrics.description: Reporter-driven assignments — bottom-up beat ownership rather than chasing trending topics
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assign and pursue stories based on reporters' beats and ownership; avoid top-down chasing of ephemeral trends or newsroom-wide reaction pieces not grounded in beat expertise.

rubrics_metrics.name: No SEO-bait
rubrics_metrics.description: No SEO-bait — refuse stories whose only justification is search traffic
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not run pieces created primarily to capture search queries; prioritize inherent editorial value over potential traffic spikes.

rubrics_metrics.name: No outrage-cycle posts without added value
rubrics_metrics.description: No outrage-cycle posts unless the writer has something genuinely additive
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid quick takes that merely participate in the outrage cycle; permit only when the writer brings novel reporting, context, or analysis that materially improves understanding.

rubrics_metrics.name: No celebrity-statement aggregation without reporting value
rubrics_metrics.description: No celebrity-statement aggregation without reporting value
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not publish posts that simply collect celebrity tweets/statements unless accompanied by reporting that provides news value or original insight.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sports as social phenomenon, not box scores
rubrics_metrics.description: Sports as social phenomenon — not just box scores
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Frame sports coverage around social, labor, business, governance, and cultural dimensions rather than pure play-by-play or statistics-driven recaps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Is this story we'd write even if it got zero traffic?
rubrics_metrics.description: "Is this story we'd write even if it got zero traffic?"
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this test to filter ideas: if the story's worth is contingent only on clicks, it fails. Prioritize pieces valuable on intrinsic editorial grounds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Would we be the only outlet writing it this way?
rubrics_metrics.description: "Would we be the only outlet writing it this way?"
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess uniqueness and proprietary angle — prefer stories that leverage a distinctive approach or perspective that other outlets aren't offering.

rubrics_metrics.name: Is the writer the right person for this piece?
rubrics_metrics.description: "Is the writer the right person for this piece?"
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Match subjects to reporters with relevant knowledge, relationships, or perspective; value reporter-driven expertise over general assignmenting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Does it deserve the reader's time?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judge pieces by whether they meaningfully repay a reader's attention — in substance, reporting, analysis, or craft — not merely by potential engagement metrics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Demoted content categories
rubrics_metrics.description: Demoted Categories — Hot takes about discourse; Listicles without reporting; Coverage of social-media micro-controversies; "Brands tweeted X" content
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid or deprioritize these formats and topics as they typically lack reporting depth, originality, or lasting reader value; treat them as low editorial priority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Elevated content categories
rubrics_metrics.description: Elevated Categories — Long-form on overlooked subjects; Personal essays grounded in specific knowledge; Sports labor / business / governance reporting; Investigations of mid-level institutions; Cultural criticism with stakes
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize long-form, investigative, and deeply reported work that covers overlooked topics or provides substantive context and stakes; elevate personal essays when rooted in demonstrable knowledge.

rubrics_metrics.name: Worker-ownership principle: labor- and attention-based newsworthiness
rubrics_metrics.description: Defector's worker-ownership produces a distinctive rubric — newsworthiness is partly defined by what is worth a writer's labor and a reader's attention, independent of traffic metrics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editorial decisions should reflect the value of a writer's time and expertise rather than optimizing for traffic; newsroom ownership structure influences what is considered worth pursuing.
